The early Newcomen engine used a large brass cylinder in which steam was condensed by a jet of cold water, drawing the piston down under atmospheric pressure.
Watt's separate condenser was connected to the cylinder by a valve, so the cylinder itself could stay hot throughout the stroke.

In the Antikythera mechanism, a train of bronze gears with hand-cut triangular teeth drove pointers that tracked the positions of the Moon and Sun.
Early integrated circuits were sealed in ceramic dual in-line packages, with gold wires bonded from the silicon die to the lead frame.
The expedition's sledges were built of ash and hickory, lashed together with rawhide rather than nailed, so they could flex over pressure ridges.
